subject: Question on combined analysis of differentially methylated cytosines in CpG and non-CpG contexts

messages.author: 67571e909b2d8a9a
messages.subject: Question on combined analysis of differentially methylated cytosines in CpG and non-CpG contexts
parts:
Hi,
 
Could I please be adviced on the following. I have 2 treatment groups. Each biological replicate within each group has 3 separate files containing methylation information in CpG, CHG and CHH context generated from the read.bismark function. My question is (1) if methylkit is able to analyse all 3 cytosine contexts at the same time comparing between treated and control groups and to (2) subsequently identify the context which the differential methylated cytosines belong to?
 
I was looking at the methylkit manual and it shows that files for each context  are loaded separately. As such, I get the impression that the analysis is centered on 1 of the CpG or non-CpG context at a time. I am therefore concerned whether I would be able to do a combined analysis of all the context at the same time.   
 
Thanks

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Question on combined analysis of differentially methylated cytosines in CpG and non-CpG contexts
parts: Could I please be adviced on the following. I have 2 treatment groups. Each biological replicate within each group has 3 separate files containing methylation information in CpG, CHG and CHH context generated from the read.bismark function. My question is (1) if methylkit is able to analyse all 3 cytosine contexts at the same time comparing between treated and control groups and to (2) subsequently identify the context which the differential methylated cytosines belong to?

You can do that (1) but why? I would analyze them separately. it will be easier to do, CHG and CHH context will produce huge number of bases, it will take extra time to analyze those. You can concatenate those files together, removing the header of two last two. You can not use destrand=TRUE during unite(). You have to later infer the context of the Cs, using other means such as looking it up from BSgenome packages, or reading the context files as GRanges objects and using %over%
 
Best,

Altuna

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Question on combined analysis of differentially methylated cytosines in CpG and non-CpG contexts
parts:
Also note that CpG methylation is symmetric and nonCpG methylation is not so (to my knowledge)! CpG methylation is also context specific (ie., varies with the density of CpGs, say islands, shores and shelves). So, it would be better to treat them separately!

Regards,
Kalyan
